paper_metadata.title: The Increasing Age of TBI Patients at a Single Level 1 Trauma Center and the Discordance Between GCS and CT Rotterdam Scores in the Elderly

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large, prospectively maintained registry from a Level 1 Trauma Center that mandates consultation for all TBI severities regardless of insurance or ability to pay. This minimizes selection bias and ensures the sample is representative of the target clinical population.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: This is a retrospective analysis of patient data collected from all adult patients with TBI that were treated at the University of California, Davis Level 1 Trauma Center between 2009 and 2016 as part of an Institutional TBI Registry.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as adult TBI patients at a specific major trauma center over a 7-year period.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Neurological surgery consultation is mandated at our institution for all TBI severities, as measured by the GCS.
items.reasoning: The use of a mandated consultation system for all TBI severities ensures that the sampling frame is comprehensive and not limited to only severe cases.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between 2009 and 2016
items.reasoning: The years of data collection are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: University of California, Davis Level 1 Trauma Center
items.reasoning: The specific clinical setting and institution are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients included in this registry were all patients seen by the neurological surgery service who met at least one of the following two criteria that prompted consultation: (1) suspected TBI due to clinical history, clinical symptoms, or signs of neurological deficits on physical examination, or (2) abnormal head computed tomography (CT) scan findings after trauma.
items.reasoning: The criteria for inclusion in the registry and the study (age >18) are clearly defined.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: all patients, regardless of age, insurance status or ability to pay are stabilized, treated and if necessary, admitted per the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA).
items.reasoning: The legal mandate (EMTALA) and institutional policy suggest that the registry captures nearly all eligible individuals presenting to the center.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: baseline characteristics at the time of injury were obtained, including age, sex, mechanism of injury, and severity of injury.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive breakdown of demographics, GCS, mechanism, and CT scores.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the follow-up rate for the primary outcome is relatively high (85% at 3 months), it drops to 78% at 6 months. The authors acknowledge that lost to follow-up introduces bias that was not controlled for, and they do not provide a comparison of characteristics between those who completed follow-up and those who did not.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: GOSE at 3-months was known for 2,713 patients (85% of the entire cohort)... GOSE at 6-months was known for 2,464 patients (78% of the entire cohort).
items.reasoning: 85% is generally acceptable, but 78% at 6 months is borderline for low risk in prognosis studies.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses the GOSE, which is the gold standard for TBI outcome measurement. Interviews were conducted by trained assistants, and the outcome was dichotomized using standard thresholds.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Our primary outcome was a dichotomized GOSE (favorable vs. unfavorable) at three and 6 months.
items.reasoning: The outcome and the timing of assessment are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Trained research assistants performed phone interviews with either the patient or a surrogate to assess outcome, as measured by the Extended Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOSE).
items.reasoning: The GOSE is a validated tool, and the use of trained assistants improves reliability.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Trained research assistants performed phone interviews
items.reasoning: A uniform method (phone interview) was used for all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The authors explicitly state that they did not control for major confounders such as comorbidities, coagulopathy, or polytrauma. Given that elderly patients have significantly higher rates of comorbidities and anticoagulant use, the failure to adjust for these factors likely inflates the observed association between age and unfavorable outcome.

items.reasoning: The authors admit that critical confounders for the elderly population were not measured.

items.evidence_snippet: When controlling for GCS and its interaction with age, there continued to be a significant effect
items.reasoning: They adjusted for GCS and CT score, which are markers of injury severity, but not for pre-existing patient factors.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: These uncontrolled confounding factors are known to contribute to patient outcome and further research is necessary to control for these factors across age groups.
items.reasoning: The analysis failed to adjust for the most critical confounders (comorbidities/frailty) relevant to the prognostic factor (age).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the data type and study goals. The authors used multivariable models and explored interactions between age and injury severity, which is a strength of the analysis.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Multivariable general linear regression models, chi-square, logistic regression analyses and ANOVA were used for statistical analyses
items.reasoning: The statistical plan is clearly laid out in the Methods section.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: When controlling for GCS and its interaction with age, there continued to be a significant effect (p < 0.001) on GOSE
items.reasoning: The use of interaction terms (Age * GCS) is highly appropriate for testing the hypothesis that GCS performs differently in the elderly.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine effects of age, CT Rotterdam Score, and GCS on categorical neurological outcomes
items.reasoning: Logistic regression is the standard and appropriate choice for a dichotomized outcome like favorable/unfavorable GOSE.
